body:
HOLDING THE REBASE. The duplicate is confirmed and the population count was
wrong — mine originally, and I am not rebasing one tree onto two branches.

VERIFIED FROM THE API, not the listing:

    #2042  bug-1420-round2   35de6d3abb540c6c
    #2043  story-1391-work   35de6d3abb540c6c   <- same object
    distinct heads across the eight: SEVEN

So my "eight of nine clear" was a POPULATION error. The method was sound — both
PRs genuinely go FAIL -> PASS because they are the same tree and that tree does —
but I counted branches where I should have counted trees. Corrected: seven
distinct changes clear, across eight PR numbers.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE STOP ITSELF, and it is in your favour rather than against:
you wrote that only #2043 has a verdict and there is no PR-2042.json. BOTH exist
now:

    PR-2042.json  RequestChanges @ 35de6d3abb  recorded_at 01:53:37  mtime 01:17
    PR-2043.json  RequestChanges @ 35de6d3abb  recorded_at 01:53:37  mtime 18:53

Identical content and identical recorded_at, different mtimes. PR-2042.json was
written at 01:17 — minutes ago, while you were composing. Your statement was
true when you made it. So the "you lose the recorded refusal if you keep #2042"
risk has evaporated: either PR now carries the same verdict, and whichever is
closed, the survivor has its refusal intact.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: picking which one lives. That is disposition — different
titles, different spec attribution (#2042 claims TASK-1289 + BUG-1420, #2043
claims BUG-1420), and TASK-1289 is guided-mode with an operator decision pending.
Choosing which spec's lineage survives is exactly the call I should not make
unilaterally.

WHAT I NEED: name the survivor and I rebase only that one, then the other six.
Seven rebases, not eight.

BOTH ARE SAFE WHILE WE DECIDE, and I confirmed it rather than taking it: both
carry the merge-hold marker AND the aida:merge-hold label, so neither can slip
through.

#1998 is rebased and its CI is running; that one is independent of this.
subject: HOLDING the rebase: #2042 and #2043 are ONE tree (verified) — seven distinct changes, not eight; name the survivor
